subject: Re: MAP & eval plan — prefetch / batching cost assumptions
messages:
From: Evan Park <evan.park@zephyrlabs.ai>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@zephyrlabs.ai>

Subject: MAP kickoff + cost guardrails

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Zephyr is excited to move from pilot to the MAP but we need to lock down the cost assumptions that feed our procurement OKRs. Two quick asks to make sure we align before the MAP is finalized:

- Can you share the baseline tokens-per-dollar assumptions you used when sizing our pilot?
- We need a short list of caching and batching behaviors that would materially change the unit cost (i.e., a +/− 20% swing).
- Timeline: procurement wants an acceptance checklist and commercial model by 6/05 to include in next week’s vendor packet.

Attachments: none on this message.

Evan
Head of Product, Zephyr Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + cost guardrails

Evan — thanks, and happy to get this onto the MAP. High level answers below; attaching a short MAP doc + the eval plan and a simple cost-model sheet that mirrors what we used for the pilot.

Baseline assumptions (pilot):
- Model: open-llm-13B quantized (int4) — baseline throughput/tokens priced against this variant.
- Tokens/$: pilot effective rate = ~18.5k completion tokens per $1 (includes caching prefactor).
- Cache hit effect: 25–30% average token reduction in pilot (prefix KV cache + inference prefetch).
- Batching: continuous batching with 50–150ms commit window; net batching reduced per-token server overhead by ~12%.

Key gating levers that move unit economics (>±20%):
- Cache hit rate drop from 30% -> 5% (e.g., many unique prompts) — increases tokens/$ costs by ~+28% under our model.
- Removing prefetching (no async prefill) — ~+10–15% cost due to lost overlap; combined with lower cache hits could exceed +30%.
- Reducing batching window (tight latency SLA) — tightening to <10ms reduces batching and can add +18% cost.

Next steps / timeline:
- I’ve attached Zephyr_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP with milestones), zephyr_eval_plan_v1.zip (eval harness + sample prompts), and cost-model-sheet.xlsx.
- Karthik and Rishi are looped for technical and commercial gating comments.
- If procurement needs the acceptance checklist in a different format, tell us and we’ll convert.

Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Evan / team — quick technical clarifications and recommended knobs to include in the MAP eval: 

1) Batching windows and latency SLOs
- Our measurements: at 50–150ms commit window with typical Zephyr traffic profile we see a 10–14% per-token cost reduction versus near-zero batching.
- Recommendation: include two run configurations in the eval — (A) latency-focused: 10ms max window (expected +15–20% cost), (B) economics-focused: 100ms window (baseline).

2) Prefetch / async fill
- Prefetching the next-turn KV fragments in async background lowered observed tail latency and allowed larger effective cache utilization in pilot. If you disable it, expect 8–12% cost increase and worse tail p95.

3) Cache hygiene assumptions
- Pilot used a 24-hour prefix KV retention; dropping to session-only (no cross-session reuse) cuts hit-rate and will materially raise unit cost. Please confirm your expected user session patterns in the eval dataset.

4) Sequencing and prompt length
- Unit cost scales linearly with average input+output tokens; control for prompt engineering changes during eval (we can add a fixed prompt template).

I attached a short notes.txt inside the eval zip with exact benchmark commands and a small script to toggle batching windows. Happy to run a quick staging job if you share a sanitized trace.

—Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@zephyrlabs.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-29T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + cost guardrails

Evan — a couple commercial acceptance points we need on the MAP so procurement can sign off: 

- Acceptance threshold: effective tokens/$ for the target workload must be >= 16k tokens per $1 under the economics-focused configuration (100ms batching, prefetch enabled, 24h KV retention).
- Regression guard: if tokens/$ drops below 14k during the trial, automatic rollback to conservative routing (smaller model + fallback) and a joint post-mortem is triggered.
- Credits: we can offer a 10% trial credit buffer if Zephyr runs the baseline eval with our harness and provides the sanitized trace by 6/01.
- SLA note: commercial SLA will assume the economics configuration (100ms batching); if you require tighter latency SLAs we’ll need to reprice or accept lower batching headroom.

Please confirm if these thresholds are workable for procurement; if yes we’ll add them to Zephyr_MAP_v1 and surface in the HubSpot deal.

Rishi
